chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about selling the juice, so it becomes wine before the price is taken possession of. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he sold its fruit to the one he knows will make it something Prohibited, there would not be a problem with that. But as for when it is juice, it should not be sold except with cash.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling fruit juice before it turns into wine?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the sale of fruit (which is permissible even if destined for wine) and the sale of juice (asir), which must be for immediate cash to avoid gharar (uncertainty) regarding its rapid conversion. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the physical state and immediate potential for change dictate the validity of the contract, ensuring the commodity is clearly defined at the time of sale. It underscores the importance of 'naqd' (spot payment) in transactions involving perishable or quickly transforming goods to prevent disputes over quality and state.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about selling the juice, so it becomes wine before he takes possession of the price’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he sold its fruit to the one he known that he would make to be something Prohibited, there would not happen to be a problem with that, so when it was juice, so he should not sell it except with a cash transcation’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about selling juice that became wine before receiving the price. He (the Imam) said, ’If he sells fruits to one about whom the seller knows that he turns it into something unlawful, selling is not unlawful. If it is juice then it cannot be sold except for cash.’”
